nodes.question: What are the seven input parameters taken into account by the model for life cycle assessment in garment production?
nodes.answer: The model takes into account seven input parameters from the life cycle stages of production, supply chain, and use, including garment design options, fibre content options, and seasonal variations between winter and all seasons.

nodes.question: Which phase of Life Cycle Inventory development primarily integrates digital technologies according to the study?
nodes.answer: Digital technologies are primarily integrated in the Life Cycle Inventory phase, focusing on capturing closing and narrowing loops.
nodes.paragraph: Abstract Purpose This research aims to develop a critical understanding of the employment of digital technologies (DTs) for LCA studies, outlining both the opportunities and challenges associated with circular strategies. Two research questions are thus addressed: (1) What circular loops and aspects are addressed when digital technologies are integrated in the development of a Life Cycle Inventory? (2) Which trade-offs are revealed in the integration of digital technologies in Life Cycle Inventory development addressing circularity along a life cycle? Methods This study is based on the problematisation approach, which critically examines existing assumptions in the LCA literature, structured into six principles: defining a domain of investigation, articulating and evaluating assumptions, develop- ing alternative perspectives, involving the audience through qualitative interviews, and assessing the alternative assumptions. A systematic literature review (SLR) and semi-structured interviews with experts were conducted to explore these issues and suggest future research directions. Results and discussion It emerges that the DTs are mainly integrated in the Life Cycle Inventory phase capturing closing and narrowing loops, whereas a limited number of cases investigate slowing loops with different aspects investigated.

Despite the benefits, integrating digital technologies into LCA is a complex process as it is still at an early stage of study and implementation (Wang et al. 2019; Sica et al. 2022). The main barriers to improvements in these terms include the need for advanced technical skills to implement and manage these technologies, high initial costs associated with the adoption of new digital infrastructure, and resistance to change within organisations (Farooque et al. 2020; Ruggieri et al. 2020).
